assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window with a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice is the kind of instrument-led discovery I value most. The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by evidence for the blazar TXS 0506+056 and for the Galactic plane, founded neutrino astronomy and bears directly on the origin of cosmic rays.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept; Karle was central to detector construction and the AMANDA-to-IceCube development; Spiering was an early leader of the neutrino-telescope programme (Baikal, AMANDA, DESY). The discovery paper rests on a large collaboration, and other pioneers (for example Baikal and DUMAND founders) could be argued for. I am working from memory on exact roles.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by several analyses and channels, and source evidence has strengthened over a decade, so the discovery is mature and the interpretation stable at the level of existence. Source identification is still developing, but that need not delay recognition of the discovery.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and other early neutrino-telescope pioneers is unresolved.
Independent confirmation of source populations (beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068) is still limited, and KM3NeT confirmation is partial.
I have not independently verified individual roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, original measurement-technology invention with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and demonstrated early strontium clocks; Ye drove the clocks to record accuracy and demonstrated gravitational-redshift and many-body measurements. A two-person prize is a clean configuration, though the frequency-comb work (2005 prize) laid groundwork and others contributed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories is strong and the technique is stable. Timing is good given the ongoing work on redefining the second.
uncertainties: Prior frequency-metrology prizes (2005, 2012) may weigh against another clock award.
Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus Ye's accuracy demonstrations is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 was the culmination of decades of detector design and analysis, validating the mass-generation mechanism of the Standard Model. The detectors are extraordinary technical achievements, which appeals to my own instrument-building background.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction. For the experimental side, the conceivers and leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are natural individuals; Gianotti, as ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement, is also strong but only three can be proposed. Collaborations of several thousand make any individual allocation contentious.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is thoroughly confirmed, with measured couplings consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is arguably late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within very large collaborations is a serious obstacle and may be seen as unfair to others.
Whether the committee wishes to revisit the Higgs subject after 2013 is a judgement call.
Choice among the four credited names is a close call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter, with wide follow-on impact in condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery (with Cao and colleagues). A theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural, although trainee contributions and parallel groups complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the phases and extended them to other moire systems, though the nature of the superconductivity is still debated. Mature for the discovery and prediction, with some premature elements.
uncertainties: Credit for the experimental discovery relative to trainees and parallel groups is open.
The mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
I rely on condensed-matter colleagues for this assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect from spin-orbit coupling and its observation in HgTe quantum wells opened topological insulators, a major conceptual and experimental development across condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original prediction, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and Molenkamp's group observed the effect. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited in this entry, so the configuration is historically incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been confirmed in independent experiments and the theory is well established, though the 2016 prize already recognised topological phases. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among Kane, Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and Molenkamp.
Overlap with the 2016 prize and with the competing entry that includes Xue (quantum anomalous Hall).
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on relative merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon strip and pixel detectors transformed vertex tracking and enabled heavy-flavour physics, Higgs and top measurements and many space instruments. This is an enabling technology of lasting scientific and practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Parker invented micro-strip detectors with silicon technology; Weilhammer and colleagues established strip detectors in experiments; Heijne led pixel development. Credit among Kemmer, Hyams, Heijne, Parker and others is debated, and Kemmer is not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been in use for decades across many experiments and is entirely mature; recognition is overdue rather than early.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely disputed and the supplied names may not be a fair configuration.
The committee may regard detector technology as engineering rather than discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes opened the TeV sky, with HEGRA and H.E.S.S. mapping supernova remnants, pulsar-wind nebulae and the Galactic Centre. It established a new astronomy window, close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Aharonian led theory and interpretation; Hofmann led HEGRA and H.E.S.S. Credit to Weekes and the Whipple Crab detection and to Hillas imaging is a major omission from the supplied names and a serious allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Many independent instruments (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS, HAWC, LHAASO) confirm the results, and the field is mature.
uncertainties: Weekes, Hillas and others are not credited here, so attribution may be unfair.
I may be biased toward astroparticle topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* test strong-field gravity and demonstrate global 1.3 mm VLBI. A remarkable measurement achievement.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging approach, Doeleman led the technical realisation, and Zensus built the European VLBI base. A collaboration of hundreds makes individual credit contentious.
assessment.maturity: Images were repeated across epochs and for a second source, but astrophysical model interpretation is still developing. The 2020 black-hole prize lessens urgency.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit and the roles of many other leaders.
Model-independent gravity constraints remain limited, so partly premature.
Possible overlap with the 2020 black-hole prize.
